Bounded completeness forbids nonzero J because backwards evolution explodes. Off the origin, u and v remain nontrivially collinear with fixed common phase by uniqueness and real coefficients, reducing dynamics to the stated 3D system. The 5D variational cocycle splits into base 3D block and a 2D transverse imaginary block along each fixed-phase orbit. On any non-equilibrium compact ergodic measure the flow vector and rotational group tangent each have exponent 0 (Poincaré recurrence and Oseledets existence), and the remaining 2D transverse exponent equals its constant trace −σ−1. The other two base exponents sum to constant divergence −σ−1−β, so at most one can be positive. Independent exact symbolic polynomial computation checked J decay, both divergences and transverse trace. It does not apply to Caputo orders α<1, arbitrary unbounded trajectories, or finite-time numerical exponents; the theorem does not prove absence of all chaos.
